Sara (support): FYI customer MaplePay (acct: maple-678) reporting intermittent 504s from hosted API, started ~17:05 UTC. Ticket #12345. p95->p99 jump.
Dan (oncall): Can you paste the sample request ids / logs? Any tenant spikes?
Sara (support): sent two samples in ticket: req=7f9a3c, req=7f9a9f. They said the app sends long chat streams (~8k tokens) but usually ok until yesterday.
Kevin (cs): Customer timeline: 17:00 normal, 17:04 first 504, then many 504/timeout for ~15m. They saw ~30% errors for a short window.
Maria (eng-sre): Looking at metrics — ingress queue depth hit the soft limit and we started ejecting; continuous-batcher backlog spiked. p99 latency aligns with queue depth spikes.
Maria (eng-sre): quick metric dump:
```
metric.queue.depth{env=hosted,tenant=maple-678} = 1024 -> 4096 (spike)
continuous.batcher.pending = 1800 -> 7200
dequeue.rate = 220 req/s -> 90 req/s
```
Dan (oncall): Who pushed a runtime change recently? deploy-bot: any deploys around 16:50-17:05?
deploy-bot: deploy:eng-runtime@v4.12.3 by ben at 16:48 UTC to prod-gateway (canary 50%).
Ben (eng-runtime): I rolled a canary at 16:48 that changed the batching heuristic (batch window tightened + kvcache prefetch). It passed e2e but maybe missed a long-seq workload. Rolling back now.
Ben (eng-runtime): rollback started 17:12 UTC -> canary removed. Watching.
Maria (eng-sre): Repro hypothesis: the new heuristic reduces batching frequency for short sequences but for long-seq streams it causes continuous-batcher queues to accumulate because those requests trigger larger KV cache churn and per-request cost; combined with tenant sending bursts we hit queue depth caps and early rejects -> 504s/timeouts.
Dan (oncall): Immediate mitigations: 1) increase max_queue_depth for hosted gateway for a few mins, 2) bump batcher workers on affected pool, 3) enable forced-kv-prefetch fallback. Can operations do 1&2?
Ben (eng-runtime): Ops: I can flip max_queue_depth from 2000->8000 for the maple tenant shard and add +2 batcher workers. Doing it now.
Kevin (cs): Told customer we're investigating and have applied temporary capacity bump. They asked about billing impact.
Sara (support): They do have committed Dedicated talks but still on hosted. Customer asked for repro steps they can run — they can send back-to-back append events producing a long conversation (>6k tokens) at ~10 req/s to reproduce.
Maria (eng-sre): For postmortem we need: 1) correlate requests hitting kvcache miss ratio spike, 2) backlog vs deploy timeline, 3) queue eviction logs. I'll collect traces for req=7f9a3c and 7f9a9f.
Ben (eng-runtime): Also adding a guard in the batching heuristic to detect long-seq steady streams and route them to a long-seq optimized path (no-tight-window). Will cut a hotfix tomorrow.
Dan (oncall): Customer errors dropping as queue depth recovers. p99 back to normal ~17:30 UTC. Marking P1 resolved for now; follow-ups: rollback postmortem + runtime patch + guidance to customers with long-seq workloads.
Kevin (cs): Customer on the call thanked us and requested a runbook to avoid future disruptions (can we add a recommended config: max_tokens_per_request, recommended rate limits per tenant for long streams?).
Sara (support): Agree. I'll draft an outbound note and recommend they evaluate Dedicated or request a long-seq routing exception.
Maria (eng-sre): Notes for postmortem: root cause = canary batching heuristic + sustained long-seq tenant burst -> continuous-batcher backlog -> queue depth limit hit -> early rejects/504s. Remediation = rollback (17:12), capacity bump (17:18), runtime hotspot fix planned.
Ben (eng-runtime): I'll create an RFC for long-seq routing and a small metric hack to alarm earlier on kvcache-churn.
Dan (oncall): Thanks team. Closing thread after PM assigned. :thumbsup:
